rows.note: This is the all-purpose choice, especially when “either” means “also” after a negative statement.

example.english: I don't eat spicy food, and you don't either.
example.jyutping: ngo5 m4 sik6 laat6 nei5 dou1 m4 sik6 laat6

rows.jyutping: loeng5 go3 jap6 min6 kei4 zung1 jat1 go3
rows.note: This is the all-purpose choice when referring to one or the other of two people or things.

example.english: Either one of the two has to be on duty tomorrow.
example.traditional: 聽日兩個入面其中一個要當值。
example.jyutping: ting1 jat6 loeng5 go3 jap6 min6 kei4 zung1 jat1 go3 jiu3 dong1 zik6

rows.note: Use this when either option is acceptable or has the same outcome, as in “either one will do.”

example.english: Either one will do; you choose.
example.jyutping: bin1 jat1 go3 dou1 dak1 nei5 gaan2 laa1

rows.note: Use this when English “either” occurs in a negative sentence, such as “I did not accept either.”

example.english: I don't want either; I already have one at home.
example.traditional: 兩個都唔要，我有一本喺屋企喇。
example.jyutping: loeng5 go3 dou1 m4 jiu3 ngo5 jau5 jat1 bun2 hai2 uk1 kei2 laa3

rows.jyutping: jat1 hai6 A jat1 hai6 B
rows.note: This is the all-purpose colloquial construction for presenting two alternative actions or possibilities.

example.english: Either we go out tomorrow, or we stay home.
example.traditional: 一係聽日去街，一係留喺屋企。
example.jyutping: jat1 hai6 ting1 jat6 heoi3 gaai1 jat1 hai6 lau4 hai2 uk1 kei2

rows.note: Use this when asking someone to choose between two alternatives.

example.english: Do you want either fish or chicken?
example.traditional: 係你想食魚，定係想食雞？
example.jyutping: hai6 nei5 soeng2 sik6 jyu4 ding6 hai6 soeng2 sik6 gai1

rows.traditional: 唔係 A 就係 B
rows.jyutping: m4 hai6 A zau6 hai6 B
rows.note: Use this when asserting that one of two alternatives must be the case, often with an emphatic or exclusive tone.

example.english: Either they’re busy, or they’re feeling unwell.
example.traditional: 唔係佢哋唔得閒，就係佢哋唔舒服。
example.jyutping: m4 hai6 keoi5 dei6 m4 dak1 haan4 zau6 hai6 keoi5 dei6 m4 syu1 fuk6

rows.note: Use this colloquial pattern when either of two options is acceptable, such as either colour.

example.traditional: 紅色定藍色，邊隻色都得。
example.jyutping: hung4 sik1 ding6 laam4 sik1 bin1 zek3 sik1 dou1 dak1

rows.note: Use this for the neutral meaning of any one of two choices, without stressing that both are acceptable.

example.english: Either restaurant is fine; you choose one.
example.traditional: 兩間餐廳都得，你揀任何一個啦。
example.jyutping: loeng5 gaan1 caan1 teng1 dou1 dak1 nei5 gaan2 jam4 ho4 jat1 go3 laa1

rows.note: Use this as the all-purpose way to distribute an action or property over each of the two items.

example.traditional: 佢哋兩個每個都要簽名。
example.jyutping: keoi5 dei6 loeng5 go3 mui5 go3 dou1 jiu3 cim1 meng2

rows.note: Use this for the each-of-two meaning with locations such as either end or either side.

example.english: There is a streetlamp on either side of the bridge.
example.traditional: 條橋兩邊各有一盞街燈。
example.jyutping: tiu4 kiu4 loeng5 bin1 gok3 jau5 jat1 zaan2 gaai1 dang1
